definitions.explanation: The open-hand shape in the game janken, which beats rock (グー) and loses to scissors (チョキ). Also used for an open, spread hand generally.

examples.japanese: パー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}して→出す：01087_dasu⟧⟦{勝|か}った→勝つ：01199_katsu⟧。

⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦グー→グー：29915_guu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧パー⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{開|ひら}いて→開く：01979_hiraku⟧、⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{数|かず}→数：00204_kazu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{教|おし}えた→教える：00526_oshieru⟧。
examples.english: I opened my hand from a fist to an open palm and taught the child to count.

notes:
One of the three hand shapes in ⟦じゃんけん→じゃんけん：06520_janken⟧ (rock-paper-scissors), together with ⟦グー→グー：29915_guu⟧ (rock) and ⟦チョキ→チョキ：29916_choki⟧ (scissors). パー is a flat open hand; it beats ⟦グー→グー：29915_guu⟧ and loses to ⟦チョキ→チョキ：29916_choki⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- パー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧: to throw paper
- ⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧パー⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to open the hand flat

USAGE:
In casual speech パー⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ separately means "to come to nothing" (e.g. plans falling through), a different, idiomatic sense.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦グー→グー：29915_guu⟧: rock — the clenched-fist shape
- ⟦チョキ→チョキ：29916_choki⟧: scissors — the two-finger shape
